questions.question: The language-head arm was added after the kill line fired on the same 201 crops — how do you rule out that split being cherry-picked once you saw the data?
questions.why: The speaker admits the winning arm was found post-hoc on the same test split used for the kill decision, which is a classic forking-paths risk.

questions.question: Your live-lot accuracy is based on one tapper's own judgment across 87 lots with a confidence interval spanning roughly 53 to 75 percent — what stops that from being both measurer and grader of your own tool?
questions.why: The speaker flags 'one tapper' and a wide interval himself, which is exactly the ground-truth conflict-of-interest this persona distrusts.

questions.question: What actually stops an unattended overnight agent from merging a change that passes its gate but is wrong in a way the gate didn't anticipate?
questions.why: The talk shows gates and flags controlling merges automatically overnight, but not who or what catches a gate that itself is wrong.

questions.question: The August bakeoff median of 10.4 seconds came from only six captures — how confident are you that number would hold up with a larger sample?
questions.why: The footer explicitly states n equals 6 for that headline latency figure.

questions.question: You call the 30-minutes-a-day figure your own estimate rather than a measurement — did you ever actually log your hours, and if not why present it alongside otherwise-instrumented numbers?
questions.why: The speaker repeatedly labels the time cost as testimony/estimate, not data, right next to hard measured figures.

questions.question: You showed four different top-3 numbers that don't agree, from 65 to 83 percent — how do you decide which one to report when someone asks 'is it better' outside a talk?
questions.why: The backup slide admits the four yardsticks can't be reconciled into one line, which undercuts any single headline accuracy claim.

questions.question: Letting the swarm self-steer broke the next day and you had to keep correcting it — what exactly went wrong, and is that failure mode still possible today?
questions.why: The orchestration slide mentions this failure in passing without explaining the mechanism or whether it's actually fixed.

questions.question: The persona panel said DONE on a fixed viewport but your own phone showed it was unusable — how many other DONE verdicts from that panel have you since re-checked on a real device?
questions.why: The one caught failure raises the question of how many similar false positives went unchecked.

questions.question: Is the full experiment ledger and the replay data behind these charts public in the repo, or are some of these numbers from private logs I can't verify myself?
questions.why: The persona cares whether claims are independently checkable versus just cited by source tag.

questions.question: For the jitter fix, how do you attribute the drop between the 3x faster server and the cancel-but-keep-answer change beyond just not crediting one alone?
questions.why: The speaker says crediting only the behaviour change would overclaim but doesn't show how the two levers were isolated.
